clue.text: The Cut a feature of the old city?

definitions.text: The Cut a feature of the old city?

indicators.note: a feature of the city puts the feature after the city in the answer, the city coming first

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, the crossword's stock old city
the chin is one of the features of a face

explanation.surface: A question about whether a London street is part of the historic city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cut is a street market in Lambeth, south London, long known for its ragged street children; the whole clue suggests such a child as a fixture there, while the wordplay joins the ancient city and a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A street child, the kind of ragamuffin who haunted Victorian London markets such as The Cut.

clue.text: Always in first place — not like Tom Brown!

definitions.meaning: Tom Brown, hero of Tom Brown's Schooldays, was flogged at Rugby School, so not being him is never caned

explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown's Schooldays is a Victorian novel of English public-school life with plenty of caning.
explanation.definitionFit: Never defeated, and also never thrashed, the fate of the Victorian schoolboy hero.

clue.text: One completely filling a large dish

definitions.meaning: someone who charges, loading or filling to capacity

explanation.definitionFit: Both one who charges, fills to capacity, and a big flat platter for serving.

clue.text: Altos ruin composition — conductors may be divided by it

definitions.text: conductors may be divided by it

indicators.note: composition means the letters of altos ruin are composed afresh

explanation.surface: Bad singing by altos wrecks a piece, and musical conductors argue over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges ALTOSRUIN; conductors here are electrical ones, not orchestral.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-conducting material that separates electrical conductors from each other.

clue.text: Shrub old ladies originally planted before a feast

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the word ladies is wanted

parts.note: Easter is a Christian feast

explanation.surface: Elderly women do their gardening ahead of a holiday celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a Mediterranean shrub or small tree, a wild olive.

clue.text: Old like the walrus?

definitions.meaning: a walrus has huge long tusks, taken literally

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for aged, from horses' gums receding, and literally true of a tusked walrus.

clue.text: First of all, tie up this prize

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word all
up in a down clue means the word for tie is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a draw is a tied game

explanation.surface: Begin by tying up the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRAW into WARD, read upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or honour given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: The weed also choked Bill in the old days

indicators.note: choked means the word for also is wrapped round the rest

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: in means the bill sits inside the dating letters

parts.note: BC, before Christ, dates the old days
ac, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A plant also strangled an old-time man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' nests the bill inside the old days, and 'choked' wraps also round that pair; the surface's Bill is a man, not an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is jocularly called the weed, the plant smoked in pipes and cigarettes.

clue.text: Not all the harem is so negligent

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the sultan's household are careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless about duty, lax.

clue.text: Dismissal for those expected to remain in step?

definitions.meaning: being told to leave a job

definitions.text: those expected to remain in step?
definitions.meaning: soldiers on parade are given orders to march, keeping step

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being sacked, and literally the commands soldiers on parade obey.

clue.text: His chair may be used as a cradle

definitions.text: His chair may be used as a cradle

parts.words: His chair may be used as a cradle
parts.note: a ship's petty officer gives his name to a plank seat slung on ropes that lifts or lowers a sailor working aloft or over the side

explanation.walkthrough: The chair named after this officer is a seat on ropes, rather like a builder's cradle, used to work on masts and hulls; the surface makes it sound like nursery furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer in charge of rigging and deck crew, whose rope-slung seat is a working cradle.

clue.text: Record book

definitions.meaning: a volume with blank pages for photos or stamps

explanation.definitionFit: Both a long-playing music release and a bound volume for keeping stamps or photos.

clue.text: Beautiful old coin for auditors, I see

parts.note: the angel was an old English gold coin showing St Michael

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the following words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: the two words I see, said aloud, give the two letters I and C

explanation.surface: A numismatist admires a lovely antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly in looks, like an angel: a synonym for lovely.

clue.text: In the Kent area, detectives rejected these pointers

indicators.note: rejected means the letters for the area and the detectives are thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, SE
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Police in south-east England turned down some leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SECID round to DICES. Kent is a county in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Indexes, plural of index: pointers, as an index finger points or a dial needle indicates.

clue.text: Don't start to feel sorry for this bird

indicators.note: do not start means the opening letter of the word for feeling sorry is dropped

parts.note: to regret something is to feel sorry for it

explanation.surface: An instruction not to begin pitying a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' drops the R of REGRET, leaving the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Popular expression about firm's address system

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: about means the word for expression goes round the firm's letters

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A trendy phrase surrounding a company's public announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the expression round the firm; 'address' here is public speaking to staff, not a postal location.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-way internal communication set-up, the system for addressing people in other rooms.

clue.text: Copy one paid for working in lesson, do we hear?

indicators.note: in means the professional sits inside the word built from the lesson

parts.note: lesson spoken sounds like lessen, which means reduce
a pro is a professional, paid for the job

explanation.surface: Imitate a paid professional teaching a class, someone asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do we hear' signals a sound-alike: lesson sounds like lessen, a synonym of REDUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To duplicate or replicate, to make a copy.

clue.text: Inclination of Ulysses about to breathe his last

indicators.note: about means the American president's surname goes round the word for breathe his last

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant, the American Civil War general and president
to breathe one's last is to die

explanation.surface: The Greek hero's tendency as he is near death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Homer's Ulysses; it is the American general Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or incline, the degree to which a road rises.

clue.text: Ruin it, for example, contriving a plot

indicators.note: contriving means devising or working these letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Wrecking something as an instance of hatching a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret scheme or conspiracy, a plot hatched against someone.

clue.text: An innovation (they, not he, understand the book)

indicators.note: under stand: in a down clue the remaining letters stand under the book

parts.note: a novel is a book

indicators.note: not means the letters of he are taken out of they

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside about who grasps a text.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make it read as an aside; 'not he' strips those letters from they, and 'understand' splits as under-stand, so the remainder stands below the book in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new and original, a fresh departure.

clue.text: In public relations, one who regulates the speed of progress

definitions.text: one who regulates the speed of progress

indicators.note: in means the word for one sits inside the abbreviation for public relations

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A PR consultant who controls how fast a project moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner or horse that sets the speed in a race for others to follow.

clue.text: Boldness shown by many these days

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
these days means in our age

explanation.surface: Bravery that plenty of people show nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery, nerve in the face of danger.

clue.text: Wife is married without a party, showing good sense

indicators.note: without means outside, so the letter for married sits beyond the party, after it

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A woman wed with no reception, which shows sound judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound judgement, practical sagacity.

clue.text: Verdian characters, one a gatecrasher

indicators.note: characters are taken as the letters of the word Verdian, rearranged into a new figure

explanation.surface: Figures from a Verdi opera, one of whom turns up uninvited.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of VERDIAN (of Verdi, the Italian opera composer) are reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder who enters without invitation, as an uninvited party guest forces entry.

clue.text: Discourage the heartless in communist uprising

indicators.note: in means the pared word sits inside the turned communist
uprising in a down clue means the word for communist reads from bottom up

parts.note: a Red is a communist

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Putting off cruel people within a revolt by the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns RED into DER; 'heartless' leaves TE from THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off or dissuade someone from acting.

clue.text: Pretentious rubbish swallowed by a dramatic Cockney inspector

indicators.note: swallowed by means the rubbish goes inside the inspector's name

parts.note: Inspector Hound from Stoppard's play The Real Inspector Hound, with the H dropped as a Cockney speaker would
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A stage policeman from London's East End gulps down nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their Hs, so Hound becomes 'OUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous and bombastic in speech or style, like grandiloquent rhetoric.

clue.text: Student captivated by neat Dutch town

indicators.note: captivated by means the student is held inside the word for neat

parts.note: deft means neat and skilful
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner falls for a smart Dutch place.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is a city in South Holland famous for blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: Following 29's specialism before 21's time

parts.note: ENT, the medical speciality of ear, nose and throat, ends the solution to 29
the clue at 21 uses these days for our age, the end of its answer

explanation.surface: A sequence of a regent's expertise preceding a brave age.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT (ear, nose and throat) closes REGENT at 29; 21 is C plus OUR AGE, its 'these days'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue, the followers attending an important person.

clue.text: Councillor's wife in service long ago

indicators.note: in means the word for long ago sits inside the word for the service

parts.note: Mass is a church service
yore means time long past

explanation.surface: A local politician's spouse who was a domestic servant years back.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a mayor, the councillor who chairs a town council.

clue.text: One with vicarious authority, say, involved in dissension

indicators.note: involved in means the abbreviation for say is wrapped inside the word for dissension

parts.note: a rent is a split or schism, a dissension
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone holding power on another's behalf is caught up in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A person ruling on behalf of a monarch who is a child or absent.
